headline: Autonomous agents, web platforms and curated databases now support antibody design
label: Ai Tools For Antibody Design
summary: Recent preprints report lab-confirmed binders from an autonomous design agent and release open tools and selection data for antibody discovery.
synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is computational infrastructure for antibody and protein design, spanning execution, access and data curation. Latent-Y is an AI agent that autonomously runs antibody design via Latent-X2, with lab-confirmed binders reported for 6 of 9 targets. GYDE offers bench scientists visual, web-based access to AI tools for protein and antibody structure prediction, design and analysis, released as open source. KyDab curates antibody discovery selection data from Kymouse humanized mice, covering 11 immunisation studies and 51 immunogens. What is new is the extension of design work from individual models toward agents, interfaces and structured datasets that surround the design workflow. The items are heterogeneous: only the agent and platform entries describe direct design execution, while KyDab contributes selection data rather than design methods.
